candidates.name: C1. First-vertex lemma: rows on A_k = {f4 >= k}
candidates.statement: Let R be residual (no 6-cap, no 8-cup, no junction) with residual states f = (f1 >= f2 >= f3 >= f4). (a) If f4(v) >= k, then every cup of R that starts at v has at most 7 - k points. (b) So the owners of A_k = {f4 >= k} contain no (8-k)-cup. For k = 2 the owners of A_2 (50 states) have no 6-cup and no 6-cap, so they form an N66-class set. A_2 ∩ F (35 states) has owners with no 5-cap and no 6-cup.
candidates.proof: (a) f4(v) >= k means there is u < v with label d(u,v) = (6 - F-(u,v), E+(u,v) - 1) and d1 >= 4, d2 >= k. That is, F-(u,v) = 2 and E+(u,v) >= k+1. F-(u,v) = 2 says no w > v makes (u,v,w) a cap, so in general position (u,v,w) is a cup for every w > v. Let C be a cup of E+(u,v) points ending with (u,v), and let v = q1 < q2 < ... < qL be a cup starting at v. The triple (u,v,q2) is a cup, so by the consecutive-triple criterion (math.md 2.1) C followed by q2..qL is a cup of E+(u,v) + L - 1 >= k + L points. R has no 8-cup, so k + L <= 7. (b) A cup of 8-k points inside the owners starts at an owner, which contradicts (a). For k = 2: R has no 6-cap, and a subset of R is octagon-free, in general position, with distinct x. The map from points to states is injective, so at most N66 states of A_2 are occupied. A_2 ∩ F: no 5-cap by Lemma A(i). QED. This is the residual-state instance of the extension trick in DELTA2N20261113 Lemma 1.
candidates.capacity_inputs: N66 <= 55 (CERTIFIED, N66N20261113) for k = 2. For A_2 ∩ F, the classical Erdős–Szekeres bound for no 5-cap and no 6-cup, C(7,3) = 35.
candidates.controls: Own exact-integer code: resstate.py and controls.py. 600 random sets (seed 1: 200 sets, 3,233 points; seed 2: 400 sets, 6,584 points). Each set started with 18-45 integer points and witnesses of 6-caps, 8-cups and junctions were deleted until none remained, leaving at most 24 points. Results: states injective in all sets; (a) pointwise and (b) for k = 1..6 have 0 failures. Negative control: owners of {f4 >= 1} contain a 6-cup in 82/200 and 180/400 sets, so k = 2 is needed for 'no 6-cup'. Real 57-point residual set (THEORY310N data/residual57_points.json): 0 failures, and the bound is attained for every k (the longest cup among the owners of {f4 >= k} has exactly 7 - k points).
candidates.effect: No row. |A_2| = 50 is at most N66 (the recorded lower bound is N66 >= 50, the ETV set), so h(A_2) >= 50 - N66 can never be positive. |A_2 ∩ F| = 35 equals the classical and ETV count for its chain class. The other k also give vacuous rows: |A_3 ∩ F| = 20 = C(6,3), |A_4 ∩ F| = 10 = C(5,3).

candidates.name: C2. Forward-cap lemma: rows on {f3 = 0} and {f4 = 0}
candidates.statement: For v other than the first point, let m(v) = min over u < v of F-(u,v). Then #{a : f_a(v) >= 1} = 6 - m(v), and every cap of R ending at v has at most 7 - m(v) points. Hence the owners of {f4 = 0} (63 states) have no 5-cap, and the owners of {f3 = 0} (22 states) have no 4-cap.
candidates.proof: f_a(v) >= 1 holds iff some u has d1(u,v) = 6 - F-(u,v) >= a, i.e. iff m(v) <= 6 - a. This gives the count. Let k1 ... kj = v be a cap ending at v. The pair (k_{j-1}, v) starts a cap k_{j-1} v w1 ... of F-(k_{j-1},v) >= m(v) points. Joining the two (consecutive triples negative) gives a cap of j + m(v) - 2 points. No 6-cap gives j <= 7 - m(v). A chain inside the owners ends at an owner, and the first point of R is never the end of a chain of length >= 2. QED.
candidates.capacity_inputs: N5 <= 65 (ETV5N20261113, as recorded) for {f4 = 0}; Baek's 22 for {f3 = 0}; the classical C(7,3) = 35 for Lo ∩ {f4 = 0} (no 5-cap and no 6-cup).
candidates.controls: The same 600 random sets: 0 pointwise failures, and the owners of {f4 = 0} never contain a 5-cap. Real 57-point set: 0 failures; the longest cap among the {f4 = 0} owners is 4, so the bound is attained.
candidates.effect: No row. 63 <= 65, 22 <= 22, and |Lo ∩ {f4=0}| = 35 = C(7,3), so every demand is <= 0.

candidates.name: C3. Endpoint occupancy rows (last point, lower hull, second point)
candidates.statement: For |R| >= 2: (i) every vertex of the lower hull of R except the first point (in particular the last point of R) has a flat state (k,k,k,k), with k >= 1; (ii) the second point has state (1,0,0,0), (1,1,0,0), (1,1,1,0) or (1,1,1,1). Rows: sum over the 6 flat states of h <= 5, and sum over those 4 states of h <= 3. These are 'some state is occupied' rows, i.e. upper bounds on holes.

I(v) is then generated by labels (4, ·), so all four columns are equal to cupEnd(v) - 1 >= 1. The last point has no w, so F- = 2 for all its pairs. (ii) The second point has exactly one incoming pair (v1, v2), and E+(v1,v2) = 2, so d = (6 - F-, 1). QED.

summary_md:
## Residual half of the ES(8) ≤ 304 chain: no valid new row found that moves any open slice

Every candidate I proved has LP gain 0. The rows I can derive from chain lengths are either vacuous or leave the LP at exactly 36. The levers that remain are capacity statements that are not proved. Time box met (finished 12:45 KST). Nothing in the repo snapshot, r36 or the working copy was modified, and no Lean was written.

### Residual model as I read it
- **What R is:** R has no 6-cap, no convex octagon (so no 8-cup) and no junction.
- **Labels:** a pair (u,v) gets d = (6 − F₋(u,v), E₊(u,v) − 1), where F₋ is the longest cap starting with the pair and E₊ the longest cup ending with it.
- **States:** the column heights 6 ≥ f₁ ≥ f₂ ≥ f₃ ≥ f₄, with f₁ < 6 or f₂ = 6, give 154 states. The map from points to states is injective, so |R| = 154 − h(C).
- **Two state classes:** F = {f₁ ≥ 5} (84 states) is where a 6-cup ends; its owners have no 5-cap. Lo = {f₁ ≤ 4} (70 states) is an N66-class.
- **Rows:** the 2,650 Lean rows (catalog `source-2650.json.gz`, SHA-256 `8c7fe9ef…`, as recorded).
  - The 1,990 coupled and appended rows of v169 are not in git.
  - I used the frozen `budget34/data/frozen-inputs/s20-v5/rows.txt`, which has 971 of them besides the capacity rows.

### Main structural finding (exact logic; LP values COMPUTED)
- **Why the LP is stuck at 36:** F and Lo split all 154 states, so in a slice (T, 36−T) the two capacity rows already force Σh ≥ 36. The LP optimum is exactly 36 on all four budget-36 slices.
- **What a row must do to help:** it must empty the whole face P_T = {h : all rows, h(F) = T, h(Lo) = 36−T}.
- **Two consequences:**
  - "Some state of X is occupied" rows can never do it.
  - A single row h(Y) ≥ d closes slice T only if d > max over P_T of h(Y).
- **Thresholds on the natural families** (`probe2_face_table.txt`). Even at their ETV values, single capacity rows on these families do not close the open slices:

| family (state count) | what its owners avoid | capacity needed to close (19,17) / (20,16) / (21,15) | what is known |
|---|---|---|---|
| f₁ = 5 (56) | 5-cap and 7-cup | N(8,5,7) ≤ 42 / 41 / 40 | ETV value 41 |
| f₁ = 6 (28) | 4-cap | ≤ 18 / 15 / 13 | Baek gives 22 |
| A₂ = {f₄ ≥ 2} (50) | 6-cup and 6-cap | ≤ 29 / 28 / 28 | N66 ≥ 50 |
| f₄ = 0 (63) | 5-cap | ≤ 41 / 36 / 35 | ETV value 42 |

- **Generic cuts:** HiGHS MIP on each slice (90 s, 1 thread) keeps the root dual bound at 36.000 (HEURISTIC), so rounding cuts are no lever.

### The candidates in short
- **C1 (first-vertex lemma, PROVED):** f₄(v) ≥ k means every cup of R starting at v has at most 7 − k points.
  - This gives a second N66-class, A₂, but it has only 50 states, so the row is vacuous.
  - A₂ ∩ F (35 states) has no 5-cap and no 6-cup, which is exactly the classical count C(7,3) = 35.
- **C2 (forward-cap lemma, PROVED):** every cap ending at v has at most 1 + (number of nonzero columns) points. All resulting rows are vacuous.
- **C3 (endpoint rows, PROVED):** these are the last point, lower-hull and second-point rows. Their LP effect is EXACTLY 0: a rational vertex with 36 holes meets every row.
- **C4 (N5 row):** from the recorded N5 ≤ 65 we get h(F) ≥ 19. All open slices already have T ≥ 19, so it changes nothing.
- **Pattern behind C1–C4:** every state class I could derive from chain-length restrictions has exactly the classical cup–cap (Pascal) count. Only the classes N66, N5, Baek and N(8,6,7) have octagon slack.

### Levers (implications PROVED, hypotheses open)
- **Already recorded:**
  - N5 ≤ 62 gives ResidualBound 117 (ES305N §8).
  - By the same arithmetic, (N5, N66) = (63, 54) or (64, 53) also gives 117.
  - N66 ≤ 52 alone gives 117, using the existing (18,18) tree and not N5.
- **C5:** |R| ≤ |R₇| + |R∖R₇| ≤ 22 + N(8,6,7). So N(8,6,7) ≤ 95 gives ResidualBound 117 and ES(8) ≤ 303.
  - Recorded so far: N(8,6,7) ≤ 104 (THEORY310N L5). The ETV value is 56.
  - I did not find this split for R in the records I searched.
- **C6:** a certified row saying at most 22 of the 35 states {f₁ ≥ 5, f₄ ≥ 2} are occupied would close all three slices by LP, with values 38.5 / 37.5 / 36.5.
  - Its proof would need residual-specific structure, because the chain-class capacity is 35.

### Controls (own exact-integer code)
- **Random sets:** 600 sets (9,817 points, at most 24 points per set), with 6-caps, 8-cups and junctions removed. Octagon-freeness is not enforced beyond 8-cups; the proofs use only these conditions.
  - The states are injective in every set, and C1–C3 fail 0 times.
  - Negative control: the owners of {f₄ ≥ 1} contain a 6-cup in 262 of the 600 sets, so k = 2 is needed in C1.
- **Real 57-point residual set** (THEORY310N): my state code gives 57 distinct states and violates 0 of the 2,650 rows. The bounds of C1 and C2 are attained there.

**Not checked:**
- the effect of any of this against the full v169 set of 1,990 rows;
- the cost of N(8,6,7) ≤ 95;
- whether M(5;7) ≤ 36 applies anywhere. I found no residual class whose owners are heptagon-free, so that analysis is partial.

### Files
All in `<scratch>/agents/residual-rows/`:
- `lp_slices.py`, `probe1.py`, `probe2.py`, `probe2_face_table.txt`, `target.py`, `n56.py`
- `exact_check.py`, `exact_vertex.py`, `mip_root.py`, `mip_root_out.txt`
- `resstate.py`, `controls.py`, `controls_seed1.json`, `controls_seed2.json`
- `real57.py`, `real57_lemmas.py`, `real57_states.json`

Its 13 owners of A_2 have no 6-cap and no 6-cup, but they contain a convex octagon (a 5-cap plus a 5-cup). An independent point-in-triangle test confirms the octagon.

| k | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

verifications.name: C3. Endpoint occupancy rows (last point, lower hull, second point)

verdict.reason:
Not refuted. The proof is complete and correct for |R| >= 2. I followed each step against the Lean definitions: ResidualRanks.StartingPath/rank/labels give label = (6 - F-(u,v), E+(u,v) - 1), and ResidualStates.column(v,i) = max over u < v of (label.2 if i+1 <= label.1, else 0); Configuration.cup means orient > 0.

(i) The row needs only the last point. No w > v_last exists, so every StartingPath from (u, v_last) is the bare pair. That gives F- = 2 and label (4, E+ - 1) for every u. So all four columns equal max_u E+(u, v_last) - 1, which lies in [1,6]; the upper bound 6 holds because R has no 8-cup. This is purely combinatorial and holds for any triple colouring. At a general lower-hull vertex every triple (u,v,w) is a cup, which gives the same conclusion.

(ii) The second point has the single incoming label (6 - F-(v1,v2), 1). F- lies in [2,5] because R has no 6-cap. The written proof leaves this bound implicit; it is Lean's label_bounds.

Both rows are valid: PROVED (written proof). Row (ii) is not new to the project. It is exactly ES8SLACK P1', residual_early_occupancy in ES8SLACK/review/C6_early_vertex/EarlyVertex.lean, which is already Lean-checked, and ES8SLACK C7 already recorded its zero LP effect. The record should cite it. Row (i) is not Lean-checked.

Controls (EXACT, my own code, 0 failures):
- the real 57-point residual set reproduces the candidate's numbers: lower hull 0, 10, 14, 56 with states 0000, 1111, 2222, 6666; second-point state 1000; 57 distinct catalog states;
- 3,000 random residual, octagon-free integer sets (n = 2..17);
- 400 random subsets of the 57-point set (n up to 57);
- every triple colouring for n <= 5, plus 28,188 random colourings at n = 6.

The negative control is non-vacuous: non-hull points with non-flat states do occur. Every one of the 6 flat states occurs as a last-point state and every one of the 4 states as a second-point state, so neither row can drop a state.

LP gain is exactly 0 (EXACT, own exact-vertex code). The bound h >= 36 follows from the two capacity rows alone. For each slice (18,18), (19,17), (20,16), (21,15) I found an exact rational point with h0 = 0, sum h = 36 and every row satisfied, including both endpoint rows. This holds on two row sets:
- the s20-v5 rows (2,650 + 971);
- the full v169 set (2,650 + 1,990).

The v169 set is not stored as a file in git, but I rebuilt it byte-for-byte from git, from s20-v5 plus the audit replay.jsonl files of cuts-v6..v13 and cuts-v101..v169. Its SHA-256 de4bcceb...916 equals ES307N section 7. This closes the candidate's "not checked against v169".

Caveats:
1. These are upper bounds on holes. The current leaf rule (check_tree, tcheck, pycheck) and the Lean Excludes statements accept only covering rows (sum h >= d). Using these rows would need new checker code and a |R| >= 2 case split in the Lean composition.
2. Integer and tree effect: not checked. None of the 68 stored residual witness vectors in git violates either row (EVIDENCE).
